macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.5.1 (build 25F80)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A second app instance that calls app.requestSingleInstanceLock(additionalData)
should always return false, exit, and cause the first (already-running) instance
to receive the 'second-instance' event, regardless of how many elements
additionalData.argv contains. The first instance should keep running.


### Actual Behavior

When additionalData carries an argv array with 9 or more elements:

- The SECOND instance gets `requestSingleInstanceLock() === true` so both
  instances believe they hold the lock.
- The FIRST (running) instance is SIGKILLed. The events 'before-quit'/'will-quit'/'quit'
don't fire, and no crash report is generated.

The first instance logs:

  [ERROR:chrome/browser/process_singleton_posix.cc:779] additional_data_size exceeds payload length
  <electron path> exited with signal SIGKILL

With 8 or fewer argv elements everything works fine. But 9 or more causes this behavior.


### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Can't repro via Electron fiddle because repro requires 2 instances.

package.json
```
{ 
  "name": "esb", 
  "version": "1.0.0", 
  "main": "main.js" 
}
```

main.js
```
const { app } = require('electron')

const extra = process.argv.slice(2) // trailing CLI args -> additionalData.argv

const gotLock = app.requestSingleInstanceLock({ argv: extra })

console.log(`[pid ${process.pid}] lock => ${gotLock} (additionalData.argv length = ${extra.length})`)

app.on('before-quit', () => console.log(`[pid ${process.pid}] before-quit`))

app.on('second-instance', () => console.log(`[pid ${process.pid}] second-instance (correct)`))

if (!gotLock) { 
  app.quit() 
}
else { 
  app.whenReady().then(() => console.log(`[pid ${process.pid}] primary ready`)); 
  setInterval(() => {}, 1 << 30) 
}
```

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Arch Linux (X11, KDE Plasma 6)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Showing a message box should work with both GTK and Qt backends.

### Actual Behavior

When Electron/Chromium is built with `use_qt6=true` ([as Arch Linux does](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages/electron42/-/blob/42.3.0-1/PKGBUILD?ref_type=tags#L613)), attempting to show a message box in Electron segfaults when Chromium uses its Qt backend, which it does by default on KDE. Forcing the GTK backend with `--ui-toolkit=gtk` works around the issue. This does not affect upstream binaries as Electron [defaults to](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v42.4.0/build/args/all.gn#L50-L52) `use_qt5 = false` and `use_qt6 = false`.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

The issue can be reproduced with the following code:
```js
const { dialog } = require("electron");
dialog.showMessageBox({ message: "test" });
```

I believe it is caused by [this cast](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v42.4.0/shell/browser/ui/message_box_gtk.cc#L47) in `GetGtkUiPlatform`  which assumes `linux_ui` always points to a `GtkUi` instance. The function then calls `GtkUi::GetPlatform` on that object to get `GtkUiPlatform* platform`. I have determined with gdb that the segfault happens on [this line](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/148.0.7778.180/ui/gtk/gtk_util.cc#L214) in Chromium's `gtk::SetGtkTransientForAura` ([called here](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v42.3.0/shell/browser/ui/message_box_gtk.cc#L121-L122) in the `GtkMessageBox` constructor) when it tries to call `platform->SetGtkWidgetTransientFor`. Since `platform` is not actually a `GtkUiPlatform` pointer, this tries to jump to an invalid address leading to a segfault.

The incorrect cast was [introduced](https://github.com/electron/electron/commit/a90ccc753b4d38266323dd054db2b98a45917117#diff-cdc15022ccefb0c20c106355d1dd71bd73478671cdb3efbc1fe4f5dad20b9635R47) during the development of Electron 41, but I have not been able to test whether Electron 40 or earlier works when built with the Qt backend enabled as Arch Linux first enabled it for Electron 42.

See also https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages/code/-/work_items/58 and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/320788

nodes.title: BrowserWindow 'ready-to-show' never emitted when webContents.setZoomFactor() is called on a hidden window before first paint (regression in 40.x)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.4.0 (also reproduces on 41.7.2 and 40.10.3)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

39.8.10

### Expected Behavior

A `BrowserWindow` created with `show: false` emits `ready-to-show` after the renderer's first paint, even if `webContents.setZoomFactor()` is called on the still-hidden window shortly after `did-finish-load` — this worked on Electron ≤ 39.

### Actual Behavior

When `webContents.setZoomFactor()` is called on a hidden (`show: false`) window in the gap between `did-finish-load` and the window's first paint, **`ready-to-show` is never emitted** — the window stays invisible forever. This happens **even when the new zoom factor is identical to the current one** (i.e. a semantic no-op call; in our case the same value that was already passed as `webPreferences.zoomFactor`).

Observed state while stuck:

- `did-finish-load` fires normally
- `webContents.isLoading()` → `false`, `isCrashed()` → `false`, page title set, renderer fully interactive
- `win.isVisible()` → `false`, `ready-to-show` listener never invoked (verified registered before `loadFile`)
- Calling `win.show()` manually works fine and shows correct content

Version matrix (identical app code, only the Electron binary swapped):

| Electron | ready-to-show | window visible |
|---|---|---|
| 39.8.10 | emitted | yes |
| 40.10.3 | never | **no** |
| 41.7.2 | never | **no** |
| 42.4.0 | never | **no** |

So the regression was introduced in 40.x.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_ — the suppression is timing-sensitive: in a bare `main.js` with a trivial or even artificially heavy page, calling `setZoomFactor()` synchronously in `did-finish-load` or via `setTimeout(0–200ms)` did **not** reproduce; the real-world trigger is a renderer that calls a zoom IPC during its framework boot (the call lands after `did-finish-load` but before the hidden window's first compositor frame). A reliable public reproduction with exact steps is below; happy to help narrow this down to a Fiddle.

### Additional Information

Reliable reproduction with a small open-source app (MIT):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Stashpeak/SimLauncher
cd SimLauncher
git checkout v0.9.10          # last release before our workaround; package.json pins electron ^39
npm install
npm run build
npx electron out/main/index.js     # Electron 39: window appears
npm install -D electron@42.4.0
npx install-electron
npx electron out/main/index.js     # Electron 42: window NEVER appears
```

The trigger inside the app: the renderer's boot calls a `set-zoom` IPC whose handler runs `webContents.setZoomFactor(factor)` on the still-hidden window ([`src/main/ipc/config.ts`, `set-zoom` handler](https://github.com/Stashpeak/SimLauncher/blob/v0.9.10/src/main/ipc/config.ts)). The factor equals the construction-time `webPreferences.zoomFactor` (both read the same persisted store), so the call is a no-op value-wise. Commenting out that single `setZoomFactor` line makes `ready-to-show` fire normally on 40–42; restoring it suppresses the event again — bisected via env-flag toggles of individual boot steps, this one line is the sole trigger.

Workaround we shipped (works): skip same-value `setZoomFactor` calls, plus a `did-finish-load` + timeout fallback that shows the window if `ready-to-show` never arrives — https://github.com/Stashpeak/SimLauncher/pull/487.

User impact before the workaround: app "starts minimized"/invisible reports from production users, since the standard anti-flash pattern (`show: false` + show on `ready-to-show`) never shows the window.

nodes.title: Support for Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

[Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC)](https://blog.google/security/protecting-cookies-with-device-bound-session-credentials/) is a Chromium feature that binds session cookies to a device-specific cryptographic key, mitigating cookie theft. DBSC shipped as enabled-by-default in Chromium 150, and works correctly in Chrome Dev (currently Chromium 151).

However, DBSC does not appear to function in Electron 43.0.0-beta.1 (which bundles Chromium 150). When a server responds with a `Secure-Session-Registration` header, Electron never initiates the DBSC registration flow; i.e., no request is made to the server's registration endpoint. The "Device bound sessions" panel present in Chrome Dev's DevTools (Application tab) is also absent in Electron's DevTools. The feature appears to be entirely non-functional.

I've tested both with and without explicit feature flags (`--enable-features=DeviceBoundSessions,DeviceBoundSessionsDevTools,EnableBoundSessionCredentialsSoftwareKeysForManualTesting,PersistDeviceBoundSessions`) with no change in behavior. The same server setup works correctly in Chrome Dev, where the registration endpoint is called and the session is bound as expected.

Environment:
- Electron 43.0.0-beta.1
- macOS Tahoe 26.5

### Proposed Solution

Enable DBSC support in Electron, matching the behavior of Chromium 150+. Specifically:
- Honor `Secure-Session-Registration` and `Secure-Session-Challenge` response headers to initiate the registration and refresh flows.
- Create and manage device-bound keys via the platform's secure key storage (Secure Enclave on macOS, TPM on Windows).
- Include `Sec-Secure-Session-Id` and `Secure-Session-Response` headers on subsequent requests for bound sessions.

Ideally this would work out of the box, as it does in Chrome, without requiring feature flags.

### Alternatives Considered

- Enabling via Chromium feature flags: Attempted with both Electron 42 and 43 using various combinations of `--enable-features flags`. No effect.
- Implementing session binding at the application level: This would require managing cryptographic keys and intercepting network requests manually, defeating the purpose of a browser-native solution and losing the security guarantees of platform-level key storage.

### Additional Information

- DBSC is particularly relevant for Electron apps that handle sensitive authenticated sessions, as it provides protection against cookie theft/exfiltration attacks.
- It's unclear whether DBSC is intentionally excluded from Electron's Chromium build or unintentionally non-functional. Any guidance on status or planned support would be appreciated.

In the shared gist I use browser API, but the same can be observed if you use Electron API for [navigation history](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/navigation-history).

### Actual Behavior

Browser Window title is not updated and `page-title-updated` event is not fired.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/Bloomca/9e89d2ab65ef82aa3e00839baf2b1240

### Additional Information

It can be a regression in https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/44144, which from my understanding intends to preserve manually set title via `browserWindow.setTitle()`.  There is also seems to be a [Chromium bug](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/40749275) and this codebase has a workaround for it (seems to have a [task for it](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/46045)).

This probably affects every platform but I reproduced and tested it on Windows first, so I am reporting as a Windows problem.

I’m interested in working on a fix and can open a PR with a regression test. Just let me know if you want that and I will work on it.

nodes.title: EventTarget.dispatchEvent() silently invokes zero listeners in a renderer when it coincides with a Debugger.pause (breakpoint) transition
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.3.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 25H2 x64

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

A `"message"` event dispatched via `EventTarget.dispatchEvent()` should always invoke its registered listeners.

### Actual Behavior

In a renderer with `nodeIntegration: true`, when `dispatchEvent()` is called **from a Node.js `net` socket `'data'` callback** and the call **coincides with the V8 inspector transitioning into a paused state** (a breakpoint being hit, or `Debugger.pause` via DevTools / the DevTools Protocol), `dispatchEvent()`:

- returns `true` (i.e. runs to completion), but
- **invokes none of the registered listeners** — even listeners that are never removed,

while a **plain function call on the very next line still executes**. So the JS thread is not frozen; specifically the *listener-invocation* step inside `dispatchEvent` is skipped.

Observed log (the anomaly always lands immediately after a pause is issued):

```
[main] Debugger.pause #857
[renderer] *** ANOMALY *** msg-17032: dispatchEvent returned notCanceled=true, but EventTarget listeners did NOT run (internal=false, external=false); plain callback ran=true. [message #17032]
```

- `notCanceled=true` — the dispatch algorithm completed normally.
- `internal=false external=false` — neither registered `"message"` listener ran (no `removeEventListener` is ever called; tracked listener count stays at 2).
- `plain callback ran=true` — the direct `onMessage(msg)` call on the next line executed.

This was originally hit in a real app where protobuf messages arriving over a socket were decoded and "dispatched" but the registered handlers never ran — **only while debugging with breakpoints**. It is intermittent: the drop happens only when a `dispatchEvent` call lands on a pause transition (observed anywhere from ~40 to ~860 pauses into a run).


### Testcase Gist URL

https://github.com/rconde01/electron-intermittent-dispatch-event-bug

### Additional Information

### How to run

```sh
npm install
npm start
```

The app opens a hidden renderer (`nodeIntegration: true`, `contextIsolation: false`) running a `MessageSocket extends EventTarget` pipe **server**; the main process streams length-prefixed messages to it and repeatedly issues `Debugger.pause`/`Debugger.resume` via `webContents.debugger`. For each message the renderer dispatches a `CustomEvent` and also calls a plain callback, then reports an `*** ANOMALY ***` if `dispatchEvent` returned but the listeners didn't run. It exits `0` and prints `REPRODUCED: …` on the first anomaly, or exits `1` after the timeout.

It is timing-sensitive — **if a run times out, run it again** (a clean run does not mean the bug is absent). Tunables are at the top of `main.js`.

## Additional Information

### It is not a V8/Node bug — it requires Blink

A pure-Node control (`node-only/` in the testcase) runs the identical logic — a `net` server, `class … extends EventTarget`, `dispatchEvent` per message — with a Worker thread driving the V8 inspector against the main thread (`inspector.Session.connectToMainThread()` + `Debugger.pause`/`resume`). Run under Electron's own bundled Node via `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` — i.e. **the same V8 build (14.8) as the failing renderer, without Blink** — it does **not** reproduce:

| Configuration | V8 | Real main-thread pauses | Anomalies |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Electron renderer (Blink) | 14.8 (Electron 42.3.3) | hit at pause #857 | **reproduces** |
| Pure Node, same V8, no Blink (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`) | 14.8 | ~1,900 across two 5-min runs | **0** |

Node's `EventTarget` invokes listeners as plain JS calls, and a V8 inspector pause suspends the isolate at a safepoint without skipping that invocation. The skip appears specific to **Blink's** DOM event-dispatch path — presumably a guard that refuses to enter a fresh listener callframe while the isolate is transitioning into the inspector-paused state — so `dispatchEvent` returns having invoked no listeners while the already-running caller frame continues.

To run the control:

```sh
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 npx electron node-only/repro.js   # same V8 as renderer, no Blink
# or any system Node:
node node-only/repro.js
```

### Versions reproduced on

| Electron | Chromium | V8 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 42.3.3 (latest stable) | 148.0.7778.218 | 14.8.178.28 |
| 41.x | 146.0.7680.72 | 14.6.202.11 |

(Exact build versions print as the `[env]` line at the top of every run.)

### Workaround

Do not route socket data through `EventTarget`/`dispatchEvent`. A plain callback (or any direct function call) is unaffected — note `plain callback ran=true` on the very message where the listeners were skipped. Replacing the `dispatchEvent("message")` hop with a direct callback fully resolved the dropped messages in the original application.

nodes.title: app.dock.bounce('critical') bounce frequency diminishes on macOS after ~1 minute in background
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist
- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker — similar to #21714 but distinct (this is throttling, not a complete stop)

### Electron Version
39.8.10

### Operating System
macOS

### Operating System Version
macOS 26.3.1 (Tahoe)

### Arch
arm64 (Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version
Unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?
n/a (dock bounce is macOS-native)

### Expected Behavior
Calling `app.dock.bounce('critical')` once while the app is in the background should bounce the dock icon continuously until the app becomes active or the request is cancelled.

### Actual Behavior
The dock icon bounces continuously for ~1 minute, then visibly drops to ~2 bounces per minute even though the app has not been activated and no focus events fire. Restarting the bounce on an interval (calling `cancelBounce()` then `bounce('critical')` every 3s) keeps it alive but macOS still throttles to ~2 bounces per minute after the first minute. Each call succeeds and returns a valid ID. No Electron focus events (`mainWindow.on('focus')`, `app.on('browser-window-focus')`, `app.on('activate')`, `mainWindow.on('show')`) fire when the throttling occurs.

### Testcase Gist URL
https://gist.github.com/Noitidart/1f1ab3a4c8002da2550818d4155eb7b9

### Additional Information
Other apps have reported related bouncing issues (Signal Desktop #652, Mattermost Desktop #693) but report a complete stop rather than throttling — possibly because they do not restart the bounce on an interval as we do.
